clue.text: Do not attend church service when drunk or collection when disorderly

indicators.note: a drunk slurs his esses into 'sh', so the phrase is said in a tipsy voice

parts.note: to not attend Mass is to miss Mass

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is told not to skip Mass while drunk, nor to make a mess of the collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS MASS, slurred by a drunk with every S coming out as SH, becomes MISHMASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, a muddled assortment of things.

clue.text: President sounds sustained by it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Emmanuel ..., President of France
second meaning: the bar over a vowel marking it as long

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads like a riddle; it describes the diacritic placed over a vowel to show it is held long.
explanation.definitionFit: The French head of state shares his surname with the horizontal mark showing a lengthened vowel.

clue.text: Silly cat among pigs?

indicators.note: the cat sits in the midst of the pigs' home, so it goes inside

parts.note: a sty is where pigs are kept, standing for them here

explanation.surface: A daft moggy wandering among the swine.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is a British informal adjective meaning scatterbrained or absent-minded.

clue.text: Spell please

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a charm or incantation
second meaning: what children are told is the polite word that gets results

explanation.walkthrough: Reads like an instruction to spell something politely; both words are definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation like abracadabra is one, and parents call the polite request word one too.

clue.text: Leaping into little retail outlet? No, a big one!

definitions.text: retail outlet? No, a big one

indicators.note: the leaping goes into the little, so one word sits inside the other

explanation.surface: Someone bounding into a tiny shop is corrected: it is not a small one but a huge one.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives a small shop with hopping inside; the definition then insists the outlet is not little but big.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping mall is a large complex housing many stores, a big retail venue.

clue.text: Walk and talk aimlessly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a leisurely hike in the countryside
second meaning: to speak at length without focus

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one wandering activity, but the verb covers both walking and talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a leisurely country hike and a long, wandering speech.

clue.text: Home origins of Anne Brontë poem

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: The roots of a poem by Anne Brontë about home.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Blocks providing coverage of ghastly Love Island

indicators.note: the outer word covers, or wraps around, the others

parts.note: bars block a way, so blocks means bars
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Blocks of ice hiding the dreadful TV dating show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a reality show, which tempts you to read the last three words together; Love is O and Island alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Tiny tree developing all the time

indicators.note: a growing tree is developing, so its letters change shape into a new word

explanation.surface: A small sapling slowly grows over the ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, the whole of time without end.

clue.text: A little money surely needed for reorientation

parts.note: surely, used as agreement, means of course

explanation.surface: Someone insists a small sum is needed to retrain or relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of course is a new direction, a shift in heading or approach.

clue.text: See 9
Patisseries getting income distributed or else

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and handed round anew, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake shop's takings shared out, or else.
explanation.walkthrough: PROFIT from 'income' is followed by EROLES, the letters of OR ELSE rearranged ('distributed').
explanation.definitionFit: Profiteroles are choux pastry buns filled with cream, classic French pastries.

clue.text: Christian starting off with a measure of whisky?

indicators.note: the word starting is sent off, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a Coptic Christian belongs to the Egyptian church

explanation.surface: A Christian beginning with a dram of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs an optic is the upturned-bottle dispenser on the bar that pours a fixed shot of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar optic dispenses a set amount, so it measures out a tot of spirits.

clue.text: China cut back Chinese social media conclusions at home

indicators.note: back turns the word around to read leftwards
the conclusions of words are their final letters

explanation.surface: China slashing Chinese social media at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like part of a news story, but it is the definition: fine crockery. 'Chinese' is only fodder for a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for fine ceramic tableware, also called porcelain.

clue.text: Dating? Must grab apartment at top speed …

indicators.note: the outer phrase has to seize the other, so it is put inside

parts.note: a couple who are going out are dating

explanation.surface: A couple who are seeing each other urgently need to snap up a flat quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Going flat out is an idiom for moving as fast as possible.

clue.text: Tunes three-wheeler for raid

explanation.surface: Someone tunes up a tricycle ready for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An air strike is an attack from aircraft, a bombing raid.

clue.text: Abstruse Euro-sceptic cup running over

indicators.note: the letters run over one another into a new order, with the cup's letters taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: An obscure Euro-sceptic whose cup overflows.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CUP out of EUROSCEPTIC and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric ideas are obscure, understood only by a small group of insiders.

clue.text: Calls up movement to do with words

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them, so calls means names
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A political movement summons people to action.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantic means relating to meaning in language.

clue.text: … shown by them getting pissed in Somerset, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form another word when shuffled

parts.note: pissed, as a past tense, means peed

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, drunken speeding drivers in Somerset are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 14: top speed is what these show. 'Pissed' looks like British slang for drunk, but here it is the past tense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedometers are dashboard dials displaying a vehicle's velocity, including its top speed.

clue.text: Carla touring East Asian country

indicators.note: the name tours around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Carla Bruni is a singer and former French first lady
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Carla Bruni goes on tour in an eastern Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: 27 is out to frolic and run naked

indicators.note: the word with is taken out frolics, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 27 across, a star symbol

explanation.surface: Someone goes out to cavort and race about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS from ASTERISK (the answer to 27) and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to dash in public without clothes, often at a sports event.

clue.text: Nomad shot real vulture, having ignored us

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as U's, two letters U

explanation.surface: A wanderer shoots a genuine vulture, without us noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'us' as U's: remove two Us from REAL VULTURE ('having ignored') and rearrange the remaining letters ('shot').
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller is someone who leads a wandering life rather than living in one place.

clue.text: Lastly, latte? Skinny or black?

indicators.note: lastly points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A barista asks whether the coffee is a skinny latte or black.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a very dark wood, and the word names a deep black colour.

clue.text: Cards from a suit or a trump to West

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means leftwards, so the letters run backwards
from shows letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bridge talk: a suit or a trump card played towards West.
explanation.walkthrough: TORAT sits within 'suit or a trump'; 'to West' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a pack of cards used in fortune-telling and some card games.

clue.text: Polluted air not helping

indicators.note: polluted air is fouled up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dirty air is no help to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like a participle, but it is the noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance or portion, a helping.

clue.text: Everybody negotiating a nice partnership

indicators.note: negotiating rearranges terms, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: All parties work out a pleasant partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union formed between parties for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Bone picked up from the last of half a dozen roosters?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.words: the last of half a dozen roosters
parts.note: the sixth of six cocks is cock six

explanation.surface: A bone retrieved from the final bird of six cockerels.
explanation.definitionFit: The coccyx is the small tailbone at the base of the human spine.

clue.text: Star in danger after moving east

indicators.note: the danger word comes after the other piece
moving shifts the letters of east into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity in peril after relocating eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star in danger' looks like the definition with a link, but 'in' is the link: ASTE from 'east' rearranged, then RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in printing.
